close_reason: fixed: next_id() already uses AtomicU64 increment (BASE + COUNTER.fetch_add); confirmed no cross-test collisions
description: email.rs next_id() uses a process-global OnceLock<u64> BASE seeded from SystemTime. Consequence 1: in tests that run concurrently (tokio multi-thread), multiple tests share the same counter, so IDs assigned during Email/set create in one test can collide in theory with another. Consequence 2: because the base is a u64 nanosecond timestamp cast from u128, it silently truncates on platforms where duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH) overflows u64 (~year 2554 in nanos). Consequence 3: contributors who see next_id() and copy it for a new object type will produce cross-type collisions. The docstring warns but the design itself is fragile.
title: next_id() base counter is process-global and not backend-scoped
